title: Independence Palace
text: Independence Palace is a historic building in central Ho Chi Minh City. Its preserved meeting rooms and exhibition spaces help visitors learn about important events in modern Vietnamese history.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: War Remnants Museum
text: The War Remnants Museum presents exhibitions about the impact of war in Vietnam. Visitors should expect serious historical themes and photographs.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Saigon Central Post Office
text: The Saigon Central Post Office is known for its grand interior hall, yellow exterior and historic architecture. It stands near Notre-Dame Cathedral in central Ho Chi Minh City.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon
text: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon is a prominent red-brick church in the city center. It is close to the Central Post Office and is a familiar landmark for photographs.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Ben Thanh Market
text: Ben Thanh Market is a central market where visitors can explore stalls selling local goods, souvenirs and food. It is a lively place to experience a traditional urban market atmosphere.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
text: Nguyen Hue Walking Street is a broad pedestrian boulevard in central Ho Chi Minh City. It provides a public space for walking, meeting friends and enjoying views of the surrounding city buildings.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Saigon Opera House
text: The Saigon Opera House is a historic performing arts venue in the central city area. Its elegant exterior makes it a notable stop for architecture enthusiasts.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
text: The Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts displays visual art in a distinctive historic building. Visitors interested in paintings, sculpture and architecture may enjoy this stop.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Nguyen Van Binh Book Street
text: Nguyen Van Binh Book Street is a short pedestrian street with bookshops and reading-related activities. It is close to the Central Post Office, making the two stops easy to combine.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Jade Emperor Pagoda
text: The Jade Emperor Pagoda is a place of worship known for its traditional decorative details and incense-filled atmosphere. Visitors should behave respectfully because it is an active religious site.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Tan Dinh Church
text: Tan Dinh Church is known for its distinctive pink exterior and Gothic-inspired architectural features. It is a recognizable landmark of Ho Chi Minh City.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Binh Tay Market
text: Binh Tay Market is a major market in the Cholon area. It is associated with local trading activity and offers a different neighborhood atmosphere from the central tourist area.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Cholon Neighborhood
text: Cholon is an area associated with the city's Chinese-Vietnamese cultural heritage. Visitors can explore traditional markets, temples and busy commercial streets.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Landmark 81
text: Landmark 81 is a modern skyscraper that forms a recognizable part of Ho Chi Minh City's skyline. It represents the city's newer high-rise development.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)

title: Saigon River
text: The Saigon River runs through Ho Chi Minh City and forms a major part of its urban landscape. Riverside areas offer views of bridges, tall buildings and river activity.
source: Lumen Travel original student guide (review and personalize)
